execution_overview.overall_summary: Executed both planned tasks in Python inside Docker. Task1 produced a significant one-sided t-test difference in log income favoring domlow==1 and OLS models with positive domlow coefficients (marginally significant). Oaxaca decomposition showed most of the mean log income gap explained by covariates. Task2 produced a restricted OLS with a positive, marginally significant domlow coefficient.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Followed the planned path including one-sided t-test, OLS with robust SE, and twofold Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition.

test_statistics.other: One-sided t-test (greater) on log(totinc): t=5.1931, p=1.20e-07, n1=704, n0=591. Oaxaca twofold: ybar_diff=0.2248, explained=0.2089, unexplained=0.0159. Additional OLS variants: Model1 domlow=0.2264 (se=0.1172, t=1.9310, p=0.0535).

result_raw.result_text: OLS with extensive controls yields a positive domlow coefficient on log income (0.169, p=0.075). One-sided t-test shows domlow==1 has higher mean log income (p≈1.2e-07). Oaxaca decomposition suggests most of the mean log-income difference is explained by covariates.

conclusion.conclusion_text: For the focal domlow effect, estimates are positive and marginally significant (p≈0.075), not meeting conventional 5% significance. Thus the evidence is suggestive but not definitive. The t-test indicates higher mean log income for domlow==1, and Oaxaca shows the gap is largely explained.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Followed the restricted OLS with HC0 SE including only allowed controls.

result_raw.result_text: Restricted OLS shows a positive domlow coefficient (0.0969) with HC0 SE, marginally significant at p≈0.056.

conclusion.conclusion_text: The restricted model yields a positive domlow effect on log income, marginal at the 10% level but not at 5%, indicating suggestive but inconclusive evidence.
